Issue 18:
# 18 — Fix checkout: Edge Function auth failure

Status: needs-triage
Type: AFK

## What to build

The checkout page fails with "Failed to send a request to the Edge Function" when the user submits the customer info form. The root cause is that `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in `.env` is in the new Supabase `sb_publishable_` format, which the Supabase Edge Function relay rejects with `UNAUTHORIZED_INVALID_JWT_FORMAT` when sent as a Bearer token.

Investigate and fix the auth so that `supabase.functions.invoke('create-payment-intent')` succeeds from the browser.

## Diagnosis so far

- Edge Function IS deployed and reachable (curl returns a response, not a 404)
- Curl with `Authorization: Bearer sb_publishable_xxx` → `{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED_INVALID_JWT_FORMAT","message":"Invalid JWT"}`
- The anon key in `.env` (`sb_publishable_iOnX9e4SdwFJf7lrW63Kug__oaNlmFb`) is the new Supabase publishable key format, NOT the legacy JWT (`eyJ...`)
- Installed supabase-js version: `2.105.1`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `supabase.functions.invoke('create-payment-intent')` succeeds from the checkout page (no "Failed to send a request" error)
- [ ] The Stripe Payment Element mounts after submitting customer info
- [ ] End-to-end checkout works with Stripe test card `4242 4242 4242 4242`
- [ ] `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in `.env` is updated if the key needed to change

## Investigation steps (try in order)

1. **Check Supabase dashboard for legacy JWT key:** Settings → API → look for an `anon` key in `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...` format. If present, replace `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` in `.env` and restart dev server.

2. **Check supabase-js compatibility:** Confirm whether supabase-js v2.105+ transparently handles `sb_publishable_` keys for Edge Function calls. Check the [supabase-js changelog](https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js/releases) for notes on the new key format.

3. **Check Edge Function JWT verification setting:** In Supabase Dashboard → Edge Functions → `create-payment-intent` → settings, there may be a toggle to allow unauthenticated (no JWT required) invocations. If the function should be publicly callable, disabling JWT verification is the correct fix — the function already validates inputs internally.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

Issue 19:
# 19 — Extract normaliseProduct to products lib

Status: needs-triage
Type: AFK

## What to build

`MostLoved.jsx` manually remaps DB view fields (`product_id → id`, `product_name → name`) before passing data to `ProductCard`. This transform is invisible at `ProductCard`'s interface — if the view changes, components break silently. Extract a `normaliseProduct(row)` function to `src/lib/products.js` so every caller uses the same shape contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/lib/products.js` exists and exports `normaliseProduct(row)` that maps the `most_loved_products` view row shape to the `ProductCard` expected shape (`{ id, name, description, price, image_url, tags, is_available }`)
- [ ] `MostLoved.jsx` uses `normaliseProduct` instead of inline field mapping
- [ ] `ProductCard.jsx` has a JSDoc comment documenting the expected product shape
- [ ] Unit tests for `normaliseProduct` cover: full row mapping, missing optional fields default gracefully
- [ ] No existing tests broken

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

plan.sprint_goal: Fix Edge Function auth failure blocking checkout and extract normaliseProduct utility to enforce a stable ProductCard data contract

dev1.task: Fix the checkout Edge Function auth failure (Issue 18): In Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API, retrieve the legacy JWT anon key (eyJ... format). Replace VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in .env with the legacy JWT key and restart the dev server. If no legacy key exists, go to Supabase Dashboard → Edge Functions → create-payment-intent → Settings and disable JWT verification (the function validates inputs internally). Verify supabase.functions.invoke('create-payment-intent') succeeds from src/pages/Checkout.jsx, the Stripe PaymentElement mounts after customer info submission, and end-to-end checkout completes with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242. Document which fix was applied in a comment at the top of src/lib/supabase.js.
dev1.context_needed: src/pages/Checkout.jsx (the two-step checkout flow and how supabase.functions.invoke is called), src/lib/supabase.js (Supabase client initialisation and current VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY usage), .env (current key format). The Edge Function at supabase/functions/create-payment-intent/index.ts expects {items: {product_id, quantity}[], customer: {name, email, street, city, postal_code, country}} and returns {clientSecret}. CartContext items shape is [{id, name, price (cents), image_url, quantity}] — note id must be mapped to product_id when calling the Edge Function.

dev2.task: Extract normaliseProduct utility (Issue 19): Create src/lib/products.js exporting normaliseProduct(row) that maps most_loved_products view row shape {product_id, product_name, description, price, image_url, tags, is_available} to the ProductCard expected shape {id, name, description, price, image_url, tags, is_available}. Missing optional fields (description, tags, image_url) must default gracefully (empty string / empty array / null). Update src/components/MostLoved.jsx to import and use normaliseProduct instead of inline field mapping. Add a JSDoc comment to src/components/ProductCard.jsx documenting the expected product prop shape. Write unit tests in src/lib/products.test.js covering: full row mapping correctness, missing optional fields default to safe values, id and name are always mapped from product_id and product_name.
dev2.context_needed: src/components/MostLoved.jsx (current inline field mapping to replace), src/hooks/useMostLoved.js (data shape returned from most_loved_products view), src/components/ProductCard.jsx (all props it reads so JSDoc is complete), supabase/migrations/004_most_loved_view.sql (authoritative column names in the view). CartContext items shape is [{id, name, price, image_url, quantity}] — confirm normaliseProduct output aligns with this shape so ProductCard works in both gallery and most-loved contexts.

plan.shared_types: ProductCard expected shape: { id: string, name: string, description: string, price: number (integer cents), image_url: string | null, tags: string[], is_available: boolean }. most_loved_products view row shape: { product_id: string, product_name: string, description: string, price: number, image_url: string | null, tags: string[], is_available: boolean }. normaliseProduct(row) maps product_id→id and product_name→name; all other fields pass through unchanged.
